title: DETRs Beat YOLOs on Real-time Object Detection

problem.summary: YOLO-style real-time detectors depend on NMS post-processing whose two thresholds slow inference and destabilize speed and accuracy, while DETR-family detectors eliminate NMS but are too computationally expensive for real time; existing query selection also picks encoder features by classification score alone, ignoring localization quality.
statements: NMS post-processing slows inference and introduces hyperparameters that make both speed and accuracy unstable across scenarios.
DETRs have high computational cost and do not achieve real-time inference, so their NMS-free design brings no speed advantage in practice.
Multi-scale feature interaction makes the Transformer encoder the computational bottleneck of DETR.
Classification-score query selection admits encoder features with low localization confidence, injecting uncertainty into decoder initialization.

evidence.quote: However, we observe that the speed and accuracy of YOLOs are negatively affected by the NMS.

However, these detectors typically require Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) for post-processing, which not only slows down the inference speed but also introduces hyperparameters that cause instability in both the speed and accuracy.
However, their high computational cost prevents them from meeting real-time detection requirements, so the NMS-free architecture does not demonstrate an inference speed advantage.

This inevitably results in encoder features with low localization confidence being selected as initial queries, thus leading to a considerable level of uncertainty and hurting the performance of DETRs.

background.summary: RT-DETR is grounded in the DETR line (DETR, Deformable-DETR, DAB/Conditional/Anchor DETR, DN-DETR, DINO) and in the YOLO real-time lineage; the paper's gap analysis is that DETR encoders dominate FLOPs while contributing little AP, and that no prior DETR was designed for real-time detection.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: origin of the end-to-end one-to-one set prediction pipeline RT-DETR builds on
relatedWork.quote: Particularly, DETR eliminates the hand-crafted anchor and NMS components.

relatedWork.name: Deformable-DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior work adding multi-scale features and query selection, whose encoder cost RT-DETR redesigns
relatedWork.quote: Deformable-DETR [45] accelerates training convergence with multi-scale features by enhancing the efficiency of the attention mechanism.

relatedWork.name: Efficient DETR / Sparse DETR
relatedWork.relation: prior attempts at reducing DETR computational cost
relatedWork.quote: Efficient DETR [42] and Sparse DETR [33] reduce the computational cost by reducing the number of encoder and decoder layers or the number of updated queries.

relatedWork.name: YOLO series
relatedWork.relation: real-time baselines RT-DETR aims to outperform in both speed and accuracy
relatedWork.quote: YOLOv1 [31] is the first CNN-based one-stage object detector to achieve true real-time object detection.

relatedWork.name: DINO
relatedWork.relation: source of mixed query selection and of RT-DETR's decoder training recipe
relatedWork.quote: DINO [44] suggests the mixed query selection to help better initialize queries.

evidence.quote: the encoder accounts for 49% of the GFLOPs but contributes only 11% of the AP in Deformable-DETR
Current DETRs are still computationally intensive and are not designed to detect in real time.

solution.summary: RT-DETR is a real-time end-to-end detector with an efficient hybrid encoder that decouples intra-scale interaction (AIFI, self-attention on the highest-level feature only) from cross-scale fusion (CCFF, CNN/RepConv blocks), plus uncertainty-minimal query selection that explicitly minimizes the discrepancy between localization and classification predictions of selected encoder features.
solution.approach: Replace the multi-scale Transformer encoder with a hybrid AIFI+CCFF encoder and select decoder queries by explicitly minimizing epistemic uncertainty between localization and classification heads.
components: efficient hybrid encoder: AIFI (attention-based intra-scale interaction on S5) and CCFF (CNN-based cross-scale fusion with RepConv fusion blocks)
uncertainty-minimal query selection over the top-300 encoder features
Transformer decoder with auxiliary prediction heads and bipartite matching
flexible speed tuning by changing the number of decoder layers without retraining
scaled RT-DETR variants using ResNet-18/34/50/101 backbones

evidence.quote: we design an efficient hybrid encoder to replace the vanilla Transformer encoder, which significantly improves inference speed by decoupling the intra-scale interaction and cross-scale fusion of features with different scales.
RT-DETR consists of a backbone, an efficient hybrid encoder, and a Transformer decoder with auxiliary prediction heads.
AIFI and CCFF are the two modules designed into our hybrid encoder.

we propose the uncertainty minimal query selection scheme, which explicitly constructs and optimizes the epistemic uncertainty to model the joint latent variable of encoder features, thereby providing high-quality queries for the decoder.
the speed of RT-DETR supports flexible adjustment by adjusting the number of decoder layers

experiments.summary: Evaluation is on COCO val2017 with TensorRT FP16 speed on a T4 GPU under a new end-to-end speed benchmark that includes NMS time, comparing against YOLOv5/6/7/8, PP-YOLOE and DETR variants; ablations cover encoder variants, query selection schemes and decoder layer counts, plus Objects365 pre-training.

evidence.quote: Our RT-DETR-R50 / R101 achieves 53.1% / 54.3% AP on COCO and 108 / 74 FPS on T4 GPU, outperforming previously advanced YOLOs in both speed and accuracy.
Compared to DINO-Deformable-DETR-R50, RT-DETR-R50 improves the accuracy by 2.2% AP and the speed by 21 times (108 FPS vs 5 FPS), both of which are significantly improved.
the uncertaintyminimal query selection achieves an improvement of 0.8% AP (48.7% AP vs 47.9% AP).
variant E delivers 1.5% AP improvement over D.

limitations.summary: RT-DETR still shares the small-object weakness of DETR-family detectors: it trails the strongest YOLO models on AP_S, and the authors state this remains to be addressed.
items: Small-object accuracy remains inferior to strong real-time YOLO detectors (RT-DETR-R50 is 0.5% AP lower on AP_S than YOLOv8-L; R101 is 0.9% lower than YOLOv7-X on AP_S).
Speed still depends on TensorRT FP16 deployment and on choosing how many decoder layers to run.
NMS-free post-processing replaces two NMS thresholds with a score threshold that still needs scenario-specific tuning.

evidence.quote: it shares the same limitation as the other DETRs, i.e., the performance on small objects is still inferior than the strong real-time detectors.
We hope that this problem will be addressed in future work.
The results show that inappropriate confidence thresholds lead to significant false positives or false negatives by the detector.

futureDirections.direction: Improve small-object detection performance relative to strong YOLO detectors.
futureDirections.quote: We hope that this problem will be addressed in future work.

futureDirections.direction: Distill large high-accuracy pre-trained DETR models into the lightweight RT-DETR decoder-homogeneous architecture.
futureDirections.quote: which makes it possible to distill our lightweight detector with high accuracy pre-trained large DETR models.

futureDirections.direction: Explore decoder distillation from large DETR models as an advantage over other real-time detectors.
futureDirections.quote: could be an interesting direction for future exploration.
We hope that RT-DETR can be put into practice.

equations.name: Hybrid encoder computation
equations.expr: Q = K = V = Flatten(S5); F5 = Reshape(AIFI(Q,K,V)); O = CCFF({S3, S4, F5})

equations.name: Training loss with uncertainty
equations.expr: L(X_hat, Y_hat, Y) = L_box(b_hat, b) + L_cls(U(X_hat), c_hat, c)

applications.detail: Real-time detection is motivated by applications such as object tracking, video surveillance and autonomous driving, where NMS thresholds must be tuned per scenario.
applications.quote: such as object tracking [43], video surveillance [28], and autonomous driving [2], etc.

applications.detail: Objects365-pre-trained RT-DETR models are presented as the strongest real-time detectors for industry scenarios.
applications.quote: provides the strongest real-time object detector for various real-time scenarios in the industry.

deploymentClaims: 53.1/54.3 AP at 108/74 FPS on a T4 GPU with TensorRT FP16 (batch size 1)
Flexible speed tuning at inference time by removing decoder layers without retraining (e.g. RT-DETR-R50-Dec5: 52.1 AP at 132 FPS)
Objects365 pre-training lifts RT-DETR-R50/R101 to 55.3/56.2 AP on COCO val2017
Trained with AdamW on four NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPUs with batch size 16 and EMA

evidence.quote: Our RT-DETR-R50 / R101 achieves 53.1% / 54.3% AP on COCO and 108 / 74 FPS on T4 GPU, outperforming previously advanced YOLOs in both speed and accuracy.
The FPS is reported on T4 GPU with TensorRT FP16
